# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/getting-started/overview

# Overview

chytr is the control plane for a workspace where agents do the work and people decide. Agents propose records, drafts, and task changes. A person approves or rejects those proposals. The database keeps the decision.

Cloudbeast.io LLC publishes chytr for technical operators and builders. There is no managed service in this version. You run it yourself: a Next.js app on top of your own Supabase project (Postgres, Auth, and Edge Functions). Feature behavior is the same on every install. There are no edition splits.

## What you use it for

- Review a queue of agent proposals, one card at a time or as a list.
- Track tasks across a board, assign them to people or agent runtimes, and close them with an explicit human gate when you want one.
- Keep accounts, contacts, deals, campaigns, and projects in one place, with an activity history behind them.
- Connect agents over MCP with personal access tokens, and wake them from desks and routines.
- Search records by name from the top bar, and ask questions over indexed text from chat.

## The app

After you sign in, the sidebar is the map. The home redirect sends an authenticated session to `/dash` unless the deploy sets `COCKPIT_HOME`.

| Section | Screens |
|---|---|
| Quick | Dash, Goals, Approvals, Calendar |
| Relationships | Accounts, Contacts, Activities, Territories |
| Marketing | Content, ICP, Assets |
| Sales | Campaigns, Pipeline, Deals, Products |
| Work | Desks, Tasks, Work Items, Pull requests |
| Support | Cases |
| Agents | Agents, Routines, Knowledge, Queues, Logs |
| Automations | LLMs, Classifiers, Decision flows, Decisions, Workflows |
| Admin | Integrations, API keys, Users, Permission sets, Domains, Approval types, KG Health, Meeting pipeline, Notifications |

A few surfaces are not in the sidebar. `/chat` is the knowledge-graph chat. Comments are the handoff inbox between people and agents. Most lists open an entity drawer for the record you click.

**LLMs** is the provider and named-instance registry. **Classifiers** edits flow definitions and question sets, and shows usage stats. **Decision flows** lists and creates flows. A new flow starts disabled, thresholds at 1.0, and the act allowlist empty (mint, enqueue, and patch stay off until an admin opts in). The path canvas and dry-run are on `/decisions/<flowKey>`.

## How the pieces fit

chytr is a Next.js app. You can host it on Vercel (a service that runs web apps) or any Node host. Its data lives in your own Supabase project (Postgres, Auth, and Edge Functions).

The app never writes the database tables directly from the browser. It calls a session API under `/cockpit/api`. Agents call a separate MCP endpoint with a bearer token. Both sides land on the same Postgres functions, so a card you approve in the UI is the same row an agent created.

Extraction is headless. There is no extraction screen. Review is the approvals API and the extraction MCP tools, on the same permission layer. See [Meetings and extraction](/docs/features/meetings) and [Permissions and API keys](/docs/reference/permissions).

Read [Core concepts](/docs/getting-started/core-concepts) for the object model, then [Quickstart](/docs/getting-started/quickstart) for the first session. Self-host install is in preview and is not linked from these pages.

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/getting-started/core-concepts

# Core concepts

## Agents propose, humans approve

An agent does not insert an account, contact, deal, project, campaign, or territory by itself. It submits an **approval card**. You approve the card in chytr, and the database applies the change. You reject it, and the change does not apply.

Some cards are human-only. Agents can file a create, merge, rename, or alias. A person approves those. Field updates and many task moves can be resolved by an agent whose token has `approvals:write`, through `approval_resolve`. Extraction types are in that agent-resolvable set. The extraction review tools, and what an approve applies, are in [Meetings and extraction](/docs/features/meetings).

A decided card is terminal. Approving or rejecting it does not reopen the same row.

## Approvals

An approval is one pending decision. It has a status (`pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `deferred`, `expired`, `delegated`), a type, a title, and an `on_approve` payload that says what to do if you accept it. The Approvals screen is both a swipe deck and a list of the same queue. See [Approvals](/docs/features/approvals).

## Tasks

A task is a unit of work on a board: `backlog`, `todo`, `doing`, `review`, `stuck`, `done`, `cancelled`. Tasks belong to a project (a desk) and can be assigned to a person or an agent runtime. Moving a task to `todo` is what wakes a runtime.

`human_approval_to_close` is the close gate. On means a person must accept a close card. Off, the default, means the assignee can close the task. Set the flag when you create the task. Wording in the description does not change the gate.

## Desks

A desk is the project a task hangs on. `/desks` shows the same projects as an org-style team view or a list. Routines and workflow templates bind to a desk so scheduled work has a home.

## Work items

A work item is the lease an agent takes while it runs a task or a job. The agent clocks in, heartbeats, logs, and clocks out. `/work-items` is the ledger. People read it. Agents write it through MCP.

## Entities

Entities are the CRM records: accounts, contacts, deals, projects, campaigns, and territories. Each has allowed fields and allowed values. Agents send those fields on a card. Illegal keys are stripped. See [Entity fields](/docs/reference/entity-fields).

Activities are the timeline behind those records: mail, calendar events, and meeting notes. Extraction is headless. A proposal is an approval of type `extraction.<action>`, reviewed with the extraction tools or the approvals API. There is no extraction screen. See [Meetings and extraction](/docs/features/meetings).

## Agent runtimes

A runtime is a registered agent endpoint: a Cursor automation, a Claude runtime, Cursor Cloud, or a Grok bot. chytr stores the webhook secret in Vault. A personal access token is a different credential. The token is how that agent calls MCP. The webhook secret is how chytr calls the agent. See [Connecting agents](/docs/features/agents).

## Domains

Domains are labels you define under Admin. Tasks, projects, and comments can be filtered by domain. They are a workspace catalog, not a second product.

## Access

One permission layer, built on permission sets, covers the app and a signed-in user's API token. Agent MCP tokens are separate: they carry the sets and extra scopes attached to that token, because the caller may be an agent.

A row belongs to the person who created it. Members see their own rows. Admins and owners see every row. The column is `owner_user_id`.

**Status.** User-set inheritance is off by default (`feature.permission_sets_users`). Creator-scoped row access is the model and is not yet the policy on every table. See [Permissions and API keys](/docs/reference/permissions).

## Workspace members

People who can sign in are workspace members with the role `owner`, `admin`, or `member`. Sign-in is an email one-time code for a user that already exists. The app does not create a user from the login form. See [Users and members](/docs/features/users).

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/getting-started/quickstart

# Quickstart

These steps assume chytr is already running and your user can sign in. Standing up a fresh project is a preview install and is not covered here.

Use your own host in place of `https://chytr.example.com`.

## 1. Sign in

Open `https://chytr.example.com/login`.

1. Enter the email of a user that already exists in Supabase Auth.
2. Enter the one-time code from that inbox.

The form calls `signInWithOtp` with `shouldCreateUser: false`. An unknown email does not create an account. There is no password field. After a successful code, you land on `/dash` unless the link you opened set a `next` path.

## 2. Create a task

On **Tasks**:

1. Choose **New task**.
2. Give it a title and a desk (project).
3. Leave **Human approval to close** off if you want the assignee to finish it. Turn it on if a person must accept the close.
4. Save. The card starts in **Backlog**.

Drag it to **Todo** when an agent should pick it up. Nothing is dispatched until it is in `todo` and a runtime is assigned.

## 3. Open the approval queue

Go to **Approvals**. The deck shows one pending card. Approve, reject, or skip. **List** is the same queue with filters and bulk actions. An empty queue links to `/chat`. On Dash, **Approvals by desk** lists the same cards grouped by desk, with inline Approve and Reject.

Approving a create card inserts the record. Rejecting it does not. Approving a task's close card merges its linked pull request, then closes the task. If the pull request is not ready, the card stays pending. See [GitHub](/docs/features/github).

## 4. Issue a token for an agent

Go to **Admin → API Keys**. Create a personal access token for the agent, pick the sets and extra scopes for that token, and copy the `cbpat_…` value. It is shown once. That token is the agent credential. A signed-in user's API token is meant to inherit the user's permission set. That inheritance is planned and off by default. See [Permissions and API keys](/docs/reference/permissions).

Point the agent at `https://chytr.example.com/api/mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The tool list is in [MCP tools](/docs/reference/mcp-tools). Register the agent itself under **Agents** if chytr should wake it. See [Connecting agents](/docs/features/agents).

## 5. Look something up

The top bar search matches tasks, accounts, contacts, and deals by name after two characters. It also resolves short ids. That search is not the semantic index. Use `/chat` when you want a question answered from indexed activity text. See [Search](/docs/features/search).

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/dash

# Dash

## What it does

Dash shows the work that needs a person, so the next decision is obvious when you open chytr.

It is the default home after sign-in unless the deploy sets `COCKPIT_HOME`. The board only calls the session API: the browser calls one session route and renders the tiles. It does not write records. You act on the screen the tile links to — Approvals, Tasks, Deals, or Pull requests.

Tiles group into what needs attention (overdue tasks, stalled deals, pending approvals, open pull requests), motions (campaigns and the deal funnel), delivery (tasks and work by desk), and recent CRM changes. A domain filter limits the tiles to one label from Admin → Domains. `all` clears it.

**Approvals by desk** lists pending cards grouped by desk, with inline Approve and Reject. See [Approvals](/docs/features/approvals#by-desk).

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role on this screen |
|---|---|---|
| `cockpit_get` | `cockpit:read` | Agent read of the home aggregate: pending approvals, notifications, and summaries |

`cockpit_get` calls `cockpit_data`. The screen calls `cockpit_dash` through the route below. Use the tool for an agent's picture of the workspace. Use the route for the tiles you see.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/dash` | Tile payload. Optional `domain` is a catalog code, or `all` |

The response is `{ "ok": true, "data": { ... } }` with `needs_attention`, `motions`, `delivery`, and `crm`.

## Permissions

Scopes come from one permission-set layer: the sets on a personal access token, plus any extra scopes on that key. This screen uses the signed-in session, not a token. `cockpit_get` needs `cockpit:read`.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own. Dash counts follow that same scope, so a member does not see another member's tasks in the tiles.

## Agent example

Call `cockpit_get` with an empty argument object.

```json
{
  "tool": "cockpit_get",
  "arguments": {}
}
```

Expected result: an object whose pending-approval count and notification list match what that token's owner would see. A token with no owner returns an auth error and no tiles.

```json
{
  "pending_approvals": [],
  "notifications": []
}
```

The live payload also includes timeline and summary keys. Read those keys from the response rather than assuming this sketch is exhaustive.

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/goals

# Goals

## What it does

Goals turn a written charter into numbers you can check, so a target is either moving or it is blocked for a named reason.

Open **Goals** (`/goals`). The board lists charters and the metric catalog. A charter is the goal: scope, title, sections, and the measures tied to catalog metrics. Publishing a new version waits on an approval. The screen can draft one. It does not skip that card.

Metrics are computed, not typed in. If a metric is not available yet, the board says so instead of showing a fake number.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `charter_list` | `charters:read` | List charters. Filters: `scope`, `status`, `slug` |
| `charter_get` | `charters:read` | One charter, sections, and measures. `charter_id` or `slug` |
| `charter_propose_version` | `charters:write` | Draft a version. Publishing waits on an approval |
| `metric_catalog_list` | `metrics:read` | Built-in catalog. Filters: `owning_role`, `availability` |
| `metric_query` | `metrics:read` | Compute one metric. Arguments: `key`, optional `filters` and `period` |

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/goals/charters` | List charters, or propose a draft |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/goals/charters/:id` | One charter |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/goals/metrics` | Metric catalog |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/goals/metrics/query` | Compute one metric. Query `key` |

The screen reads the catalog, queries each metric it shows, and posts a charter draft to the list route. Agents use the MCP tools for the same records.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reading goals needs `charters:read` and `metrics:read`. Proposing a charter version needs `charters:write`. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `metric_query` with a catalog key. `period` is `week`, `month`, or `quarter`.

```json
{
  "tool": "metric_query",
  "arguments": {
    "key": "cro.demos_held_weekly",
    "period": "week"
  }
}
```

Expected result when the metric is built: `ok` true, `availability` `available`, and a `value`. A metric that is not built yet returns `ok` true with `availability` `not_yet_available` and a `blocked_reason`, not a zero. An unknown key returns `ok` false and `error` `unknown_metric`.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "key": "cro.demos_held_weekly",
  "availability": "available",
  "value": 2
}
```

Propose a charter only with `charter_propose_version`. The published row appears after the approval is accepted.

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/approvals

# Approvals

## What it does

Approvals give you one queue for every proposal an agent files, so the database applies a change only when you accept it.

Approvals are the decision queue. An agent, a workflow, or an ingest job inserts a `pending` row. You resolve it. The database runs the card's `on_approve` action only when the status becomes `approved`.

Open **Approvals** (`/approvals`). **Deck** is one card at a time: approve, reject, or skip. **List** is the same pending queue with a domain filter, type tabs, and bulk approve or reject. `/deck` redirects to the deck view. The list and the deck call the same resolve API.

You can also open a card's chat from the deck. That chat can search indexed text. It does not resolve the card for you.

## By desk

Approvals are also grouped by desk (project), so you can decide the cards that belong to the work you are looking at.

- **Dash** shows **Approvals by desk**. Each desk lists its cards, with an **Open / All** switch. Desks with nothing to show are hidden.
- A desk's own page shows **Open Approvals** for that desk only.
- The task drawer shows the cards linked to that task.

Pending rows have inline **Approve** and **Reject** buttons, so you do not have to open the deck. They use the same decision routes as the deck and list. Approving a close card here merges the linked pull request, and rejecting a proposed task cancels it, exactly as in the deck. See [GitHub](/docs/features/github).

What you can decide follows [What a member can see](/docs/features/users#what-a-member-can-see).

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending` | Waiting |
| `approved` | Accepted. `on_approve` has run, or has recorded its result |
| `rejected` | Declined. `on_approve` does not run |
| `deferred` | Set aside. The deck and list resolve actions use approve and reject |
| `expired` | No longer actionable |
| `delegated` | Handed to someone else |

The chytr resolve buttons send `approved` or `rejected`. Other statuses exist on the row for agents and for bulk tools.

An approve must be attributed. A session in chytr, or `resolve_approval` from a token, stamps who decided. A raw update that sets `approved` with no actor is refused.

## What approve does

`on_approve.kind` selects the action. The kinds you will see on entity cards:

| Kind | Effect |
|---|---|
| `entity_create` | Insert one row in `accounts`, `contacts`, `deals`, `projects`, `campaigns`, or `territories` |
| `entity_update` | Write the listed fields and record who changed them |
| `entity_merge` | Merge the loser into the keeper. Needs the merge decision on the card |
| `entity_alias_add` | Add an alias |
| `task_status` | Move the linked tasks from one status to another |
| `row_status` | Flip an allow-listed marketing or campaign-member status |
| `enqueue` | Send a job to an allow-listed queue |

Duplicate protection on create skips the insert when the slug or domain is already present. Keys that are not in the entity shape are dropped. Shapes are editable under **Admin → Approval types** (`/settings/approvals`).

## What you send on a create card

Agents call `approval_create` (scope `approvals:write`) or include the entity on a graph check-in. For a create, send `item_type` `graph_entity_create` and either `on_approve` or `table` plus `fields`.

A contact example, with no address on purpose:

```json
{
  "item_type": "graph_entity_create",
  "title": "Create contact: Jane Example",
  "table": "contacts",
  "fields": {
    "full_name": "Jane Example",
    "title": "VP Operations",
    "lifecycle_stage": "lead"
  }
}
```

Required and allowed fields are in [Entity fields](/docs/reference/entity-fields). Do not send `tags`, `domain_wall`, `references`, `slug`, `id`, or `owner_user_id`. Do not send `name` on a contact. Foreign keys accept an id or a slug.

`graph_entity_update` is the matching type for a field change. `project_create` is a project-shaped create.

## Human-only cards

These types stay with a person. `approval_resolve` from an agent token refuses them:

- `graph_entity_merge`
- `graph_entity_rename`
- `graph_entity_create`
- `graph_entity_alias`
- `merge_proposal`
- `stage2_identity`
- `product_create`
- `product_rename`
- `engagement_outcome_achieve`
- `workflow_cross_desk_grant`

Agents may still **propose** a create. A person approves it in chytr. Agents may resolve types that are not on this list, including `graph_entity_update` and extraction cards, when the token has `approvals:write`.

Fuzzy name matches are not auto-merged. The card should show the candidates. You confirm.

## Task cards

Promoting a backlog task and closing a task that has `human_approval_to_close` set both show up here (`task_promote`, `task_close_ack`). Rejecting a proposed task cancels the linked task. It does not promote it. Approving a `task_close_ack` card merges the task's linked pull requests with a merge commit, then closes the task. If a pull request is not ready, the approval is refused and the card stays pending. See [GitHub](/docs/features/github).

## Where else cards come from

Meeting and activity extraction uses this same queue. The type is `extraction.<action>`. There is no extraction screen and no second inbox. A router card's `on_approve` is `extraction_apply` (or `entity_merge` for a complete merge). Approve runs that action. A failed apply leaves the card pending. Reject applies nothing. The contract is in [Meetings and extraction](/docs/features/meetings). Shapes for create cards are edited on [Approval types](/docs/features/approval-types).

A workflow trigger go-live files `workflow_trigger_go_live`. Approving it is what sets `trigger_mode` to `live`. See [Workflows](/docs/features/workflows).

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `approval_create` | `approvals:write` | File a pending card |
| `approval_list` | `approvals:read` | List cards. Filter `status` |
| `approval_resolve` | `approvals:write` | Resolve through `resolve_approval`. A session records human. A PAT records agent. Human-only approve needs owner or admin |
| `extraction_pending` | `approvals:read` | Extraction cards in this same queue |
| `extraction_review` | `approvals:write` | Approve or reject one extraction card |

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/approvals` | Pending queue |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id` | Read, or set `approved` / `rejected` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/bulk` | Bulk resolve |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id/merge-approve` | Approve a merge card |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id/merge-context` | Merge context |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/by-desk` | Cards grouped by desk. Query `include=open` or `all`, optional `project_id` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id/close-approve` | Approve a close card |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id/reject-cancel` | Reject and cancel the linked work |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/approval-shapes` | Shapes. The editor is [Approval types](/docs/features/approval-types) |

Deck helpers, same session: `POST /cockpit/api/deck/chat`, `POST /cockpit/api/deck/graph-chat`, `GET /cockpit/api/deck/context`, `GET /cockpit/api/deck/ground`, `POST /cockpit/api/deck/events`.

The screen only calls these routes. Agents use the MCP tools. Both land on the same rows.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Listing needs `approvals:read`. Filing or resolving needs `approvals:write`. Human-only types stay with a person even when the token has that scope. A session can resolve a card it owns, or any card when `is_admin()` is true. A workspace role is not that flag.

Row access on this table is creator-based RLS. A member sees rows they own (`owner_user_id` is the signed-in user). `is_admin()` sees all rows. A personal access token with `approvals:read` can select, and `approvals:write` can insert or update, through the token scope check, including rows that person did not create. A session that sets `approved`, `rejected`, or `deferred` records that user as human. A PAT with no session records the token as agent through `resolve_approval`. A session cannot forge the agent identity.

## Agent example

Call `approval_list` for what is waiting, then `approval_resolve` only for a type that is not human-only.

```json
{
  "tool": "approval_list",
  "arguments": {
    "status": "pending",
    "limit": 10
  }
}
```

Expected result: pending cards visible to the token owner. Resolving a `graph_entity_create` with `approval_resolve` is refused. Resolving an extraction card or a `graph_entity_update` with `status` `approved` runs that card's `on_approve`. An extraction card's apply is `extraction_apply`. A failed apply leaves the card pending. `rejected` does not apply.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "approvals": [
    {
      "title": "Create contact: Jane Example",
      "status": "pending",
      "item_type": "graph_entity_create"
    }
  ]
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/calendar

# Calendar

## What it does

Calendar shows what was held and what is coming, so a missing note becomes a proposal instead of a silent hole.

Open **Calendar** (`/calendar`). Month, day, multi-day, and list are the same events. `/timeline` redirects here. The grid only calls one session route. Opening an event loads the fuller card. A gap action does not edit the event. It files a pending approval, and you resolve that card on [Approvals](/docs/features/approvals).

How meetings are extracted is in [Meetings and extraction](/docs/features/meetings). This page is the screen.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `meeting_brief_checkin` | `graph:write` | Attach a pre-call brief to a calendar activity. Does not change entities |
| `meeting_graph_checkin` | `graph:write` | Write the meeting, proposals, links, and notes in one call |
| `activity_timeline` | `activities:read` | Owner-wide feed, including calendar types |
| `timeline_for_entity` | `activities:read`, `mentions:read` | Activity timeline for one record |

The grid itself has no MCP twin. Agents write meetings with the check-in tools, then read them back with the timeline tools.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/calendar/grid` | Events for the visible range. Optional `from` and `to` |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/timeline` | Fuller card when an event is opened |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/timeline/link` | Attach a note to an event |
| `POST` | `/api/gap-action` | File a pending approval. Does not apply the action |

Gap actions are `log-call`, `generate-brief`, `not-held`, and `exclude`. Each one inserts a pending card. Nothing is sent and no note is written until that card is approved.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Check-in tools need `graph:write`. Timeline reads need `activities:read`. The screen uses the signed-in session, including `/api/gap-action`.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `meeting_brief_checkin` with the calendar activity and the brief body.

```json
{
  "tool": "meeting_brief_checkin",
  "arguments": {
    "calendar_activity_id": "cal-activity-1",
    "run_id": "brief-run-1",
    "brief": {
      "summary": "Confirm scope and the decision owner before the call."
    }
  }
}
```

Expected result: the brief is stored on that calendar activity. Accounts, contacts, and deals are unchanged. A second call with the same `run_id` does not create a second brief.

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/accounts

# Accounts

## What it does

Accounts keep every company in one list, so a deal, a contact, and a meeting all point at the same record.

Open **Accounts** (`/accounts`). Search by name, domain, or slug. The drawer edits fields. A person signed in to chytr can create a row directly. An agent does not. `entity_create` on MCP is deprecated and does not insert. The agent files an approval, and a person accepts it. Allowed fields are in [Entity fields](/docs/reference/entity-fields).

The screen only calls the session API. List, create, update, and merge go through the session API under the signed-in user, and row policies apply.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `approval_create` | `approvals:write` | Propose a company. `item_type` `graph_entity_create`, `table` `accounts` |
| `entity_field_write` | `graph:write` | Write one field through provenance |
| `accounts_due_for_enrichment` | `accounts:read` | Companies whose enrichment is stale |
| `entity_get` | none (token still required) | Full card by search-entity id |
| `entity_state_get` | none (token still required) | Read `agent_state` |
| `entity_state_set` | `accounts:write` | Replace `agent_state` |
| `entity_state_patch` | `accounts:write` | Shallow-merge `agent_state` |
| `entity_note_add` | `notes:write` | Append a note |
| `entity_notes_list` | `notes:read` | Recent notes |
| `scorecard_get` | `accounts:read` | Latest scorecard when `record_table` is `accounts` |

Do not call MCP `entity_create`. It returns deprecated and writes nothing.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/accounts` | List. `?q=` searches name, domain, and slug |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/accounts/search` | Picker lookup |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/entities/accounts` | Create from a signed-in session. Provenance source is `human` |
| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | `/cockpit/api/entities/accounts/:id` | Drawer read, update, delete |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/entities/accounts/:id/merge` | Merge into the keeper |

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reads need `accounts:read`. Field writes from an agent need `graph:write` or `accounts:write` as the table above shows. Creates that should wait for a person use `approvals:write`.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `approval_create` to propose a company. Do not send `owner_user_id`, `id`, or `slug` inside `fields`.

```json
{
  "tool": "approval_create",
  "arguments": {
    "item_type": "graph_entity_create",
    "title": "Create account: Example Co",
    "table": "accounts",
    "fields": {
      "name": "Example Co",
      "domain": "example-co.invalid",
      "industry": "software"
    }
  }
}
```

Expected result: a pending approval. The account row does not exist until a person approves the card. Rejecting the card leaves the list unchanged.

```json
{
  "status": "pending",
  "item_type": "graph_entity_create",
  "title": "Create account: Example Co"
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/contacts

# Contacts

## What it does

Contacts keep the people you work with on the company they belong to, so a name in a meeting can become a real record only after you accept it.

Open **Contacts** (`/contacts`). The list and the drawer only call the session API. A signed-in person can create a contact. An agent proposes one with `approval_create` and waits. A single first name with no email and no account is not a confirmed person. Allowed fields are in [Entity fields](/docs/reference/entity-fields). Send `full_name`, not `name`.

`contact_intake` is the direct write for an intake payload that already has an email and a company. It is not a shortcut around a fuzzy name.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `approval_create` | `approvals:write` | Propose a person. `table` `contacts`, type `graph_entity_create` |
| `contact_intake` | `contacts:write`, `accounts:write` | Create a contact and account from an intake payload that includes `email` |
| `entity_field_write` | `graph:write` | Write one field through provenance |
| `entity_get` | none (token still required) | Full card by search-entity id |
| `entity_state_get` | none (token still required) | Read `agent_state` |
| `entity_state_set` | `contacts:write` | Replace `agent_state` |
| `entity_state_patch` | `contacts:write` | Shallow-merge `agent_state` |
| `entity_note_add` | `notes:write` | Append a note |
| `entity_notes_list` | `notes:read` | Recent notes |
| `scorecard_get` | `contacts:read` | Latest scorecard when `record_table` is `contacts` |
| `mention_add` | `mentions:write`, `activities:write` | Link an activity to this person |

Do not call MCP `entity_create`. It returns deprecated and writes nothing.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/contacts` | List |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/entities/contacts` | Create from a signed-in session. Provenance source is `human` |
| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | `/cockpit/api/entities/contacts/:id` | Drawer read, update, delete |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/entities/contacts/:id/merge` | Merge into the keeper |

A duplicate email on create returns a conflict and names the contact that already holds it. The second row is not inserted.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reads need `contacts:read`. Intake needs both `contacts:write` and `accounts:write`. Proposals need `approvals:write`.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `approval_create` for a person you are not ready to treat as confirmed.

```json
{
  "tool": "approval_create",
  "arguments": {
    "item_type": "graph_entity_create",
    "title": "Create contact: Jane Example",
    "table": "contacts",
    "fields": {
      "full_name": "Jane Example",
      "title": "VP Operations",
      "lifecycle_stage": "lead"
    }
  }
}
```

Expected result: a pending card. No contact row until a person approves it. `lifecycle_stage` `prospect` is stored as `lead`.

```json
{
  "status": "pending",
  "item_type": "graph_entity_create",
  "title": "Create contact: Jane Example"
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/activities

# Activities

## What it does

Activities are the timeline behind every account and contact, so a proposal can point at the message or meeting that caused it.

Open **Activities** (`/activities`). Filter by type (mail, calendar, meetings, other), quality, whether the row is linked to a record, and date. The list is read-only. Extraction proposals from these rows show up on [Approvals](/docs/features/approvals), not as a second inbox. The rules are in [Meetings and extraction](/docs/features/meetings).

Quality classes are `substantive`, `transactional`, `notification`, `digest`, and `noise`. Digest and noise stay out of the embedding index.

The screen only calls the session API. It only reads the session route. Agents write rows with MCP, and the same list shows them after the write commits.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `activity_timeline` | `activities:read` | Owner-wide feed. Keyset via `cursor`. `exclude_noise` drops low-value rows |
| `activity_create` | `activities:write` | Create or upsert one activity |
| `timeline_for_entity` | `activities:read`, `mentions:read` | Feed for one CRM record |
| `mention_add` | `mentions:write`, `activities:write` | Link an activity to an entity |
| `meeting_graph_checkin` | `graph:write` | Write a meeting plus proposals, links, and notes |

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/activities` | Paged list for this screen |

Query parameters the screen sends:

| Param | Values |
|---|---|
| `type` | `all`, `email`, `calendar`, `meetings`, `other`, or a concrete `activities.type` |
| `quality` | Comma-separated quality classes |
| `linked` | `all`, `yes`, `no` |
| `range` | `today`, `this_week`, `this_month`, `all` |
| `q` | Summary substring |
| `limit`, `offset` | Page controls |

Future `occurred_at` rows are excluded. `after` and `before` override `range` when both are set.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reading the feed needs `activities:read`. Writing a row needs `activities:write`. Linking it needs `mentions:write` as well. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `activity_create` for a note you already know is real.

```json
{
  "tool": "activity_create",
  "arguments": {
    "type": "meeting_note",
    "summary": "Scoped the rollout to one region.",
    "source": "agent",
    "source_id": "note-run-1",
    "occurred_at": "2026-10-09T15:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

Expected result: one activity row. Calling again with the same `source` and `source_id` updates that row instead of inserting a second one. The Activities screen shows it after a refresh, inside the owner's RLS scope.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "type": "meeting_note",
  "summary": "Scoped the rollout to one region."
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/territories

# Territories

## What it does

Territories show who covers a slice of a partner's map, so a campaign can target a patch instead of a loose list of accounts.

Open **Territories** (`/territories`). A territory is a coverage slice on a partner account: region, industry, and segment, with the people who cover it. The list and the drawer only call the session API. A signed-in person can create a row. An agent proposes one and waits for approval. There is no MCP tool that lists or inserts territories directly.

Allowed fields are in [Entity fields](/docs/reference/entity-fields).

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `approval_create` | `approvals:write` | Propose a territory. `table` `territories`, type `graph_entity_create` |
| `entity_field_write` | `graph:write` | Write one field through provenance |
| `entity_note_add` | `notes:write` | Append a note |
| `entity_notes_list` | `notes:read` | Recent notes |
| `entity_get` | none (token still required) | Full card when a search entity exists for the row |

Do not call MCP `entity_create`. It returns deprecated and writes nothing.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/territories` | List |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/entities/territories` | Create from a signed-in session. Provenance source is `human` |
| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | `/cockpit/api/entities/territories/:id` | Drawer read, update, delete |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/entities/territories/:id/merge` | Merge into the keeper |

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. A proposal needs `approvals:write`. A field write needs `graph:write`. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `approval_create` with the territory's name and the partner it hangs on. Send a slug or an id for the partner foreign key, not a display name alone.

```json
{
  "tool": "approval_create",
  "arguments": {
    "item_type": "graph_entity_create",
    "title": "Create territory: West Manufacturing",
    "table": "territories",
    "fields": {
      "name": "West Manufacturing",
      "partner": "example-partner"
    }
  }
}
```

Expected result: a pending card. The territory does not appear on `/territories` until a person approves it.

```json
{
  "status": "pending",
  "item_type": "graph_entity_create",
  "title": "Create territory: West Manufacturing"
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/content

# Content

## What it does

Content shows every marketing piece and where it sits, so you can see what is drafted, scheduled, or published without editing the engine by hand.

Open **Content** (`/marketing-content`). The board is read-only. Filter by status, type, channel, and a date window. Statuses include `planned`, `drafted`, `review`, `scheduled`, `publishing`, `published`, `failed`, and `cancelled`. Opening a row uses the entity drawer. There is no New button and no MCP tool that writes `marketing_content_items`.

Generation stays headless. This screen only reads the result. Assets you upload as files are a different object on [Assets](/docs/features/assets).

## MCP tools

No MCP tool targets this board. Agents that need a file-backed piece use the asset tools on [Assets](/docs/features/assets). Do not invent a content-item tool. The session route below is the read path.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/marketing-content` | Paged list. This route is GET only |

Query parameters the screen sends: `status` and `type` as comma-separated lists, `channel`, `after`, `before`, `limit`, and `offset`. The body is `{ "ok": true, "items": [...], "has_more": true|false }`.

## Permissions

The screen uses the signed-in session. There is no content-item scope on the permission-set layer because there is no tool. Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

There is no tool call that lists these rows. A session client reads the same route the board uses.

```json
{
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/cockpit/api/marketing-content?status=published&limit=50&offset=0"
}
```

Expected result: published items visible to that user, newest window first, with `has_more` when another page exists. A member does not receive another member's rows.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "items": [
    {
      "title": "Launch note",
      "status": "published"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": false
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/icp

# ICP

## What it does

ICP defines who a motion is for, so fit scores and win rate sit on the same profile instead of in a slide.

Open **ICP** (`/marketing-icp`). Three blocks share the page: profile versions, a fit-and-intent grid, and a win-rate card. Drafting a new version does not activate it. Activation waits on an approval, the same pattern as a charter. The screen only calls the session routes. Agents call the MCP tools and land on the same rows.

Attaching profiles to a campaign is `campaign_icp_set`, documented with the tools below and on [Campaigns](/docs/features/campaigns).

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `icp_list` | `icp:read` | List versions. Filters: `status`, `slug`, `include_criteria`, `limit` |
| `icp_get` | `icp:read` | One profile and its version history |
| `icp_propose_version` | `icp:write` | Draft a version. Activation waits on an approval |
| `account_fit_score` | `icp:write` | Score an account and write the fit fields |
| `accounts_by_tier` | `icp:read` | Accounts in a fit tier |
| `campaign_icp_set` | `campaigns:write` | Attach profiles to a campaign |

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/icp-profiles` | List, or propose a version. `?slug=&history=1` loads history |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/icp-fit-intent` | Fit and intent grid |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/icp-win-rate` | Win-rate summary |

The fit and win-rate routes are read-only. Scoring an account is the MCP tool, not a button that bypasses it.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reading needs `icp:read`. Proposing a version or writing a fit score needs `icp:write`. Linking a campaign needs `campaigns:write`. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `icp_propose_version` with a slug. Reusing a slug drafts the next version. It does not publish.

```json
{
  "tool": "icp_propose_version",
  "arguments": {
    "slug": "mid-market-ops",
    "name": "Mid-market operations",
    "summary": "Operators who own data quality for more than one system.",
    "criteria": {
      "industry": ["software"],
      "segment": ["mid-market"]
    }
  }
}
```

Expected result: a draft version and a pending approval. The fit grid does not use that version until the card is approved.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "draft",
  "slug": "mid-market-ops"
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/assets

# Assets

## What it does

Assets give a marketing file a stable name and a version history, so a one-pager can be updated without losing the copy you already shared.

Open **Assets** (`/assets`). You create an asset identity, then add versions that point at a committed file. The bytes are a file row. The asset is the name, kind, and current version. Sharing is recorded. It is not sent. The content calendar is a different list on [Content](/docs/features/content).

The screen only calls the session API. Agents use the same file and asset tools, and the board shows the rows those tools write.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `file_reserve` | `files:write` | Reserve a file row and an upload URL, deduped by hash |
| `file_commit` | `files:write` | Mark the upload ready |
| `file_signed_url` | `files:read` | Short-lived download URL |
| `marketing_asset_create` | `files:write` | Create the asset identity |
| `marketing_asset_version_add` | `files:write` | Add a version that points at a committed file |
| `marketing_asset_list` | `files:read` | List assets |
| `marketing_asset_get` | `files:read` | One asset and its versions |
| `marketing_asset_set_current` | `files:write` | Point the asset at a version |
| `file_link` | `files:write` | Link a file to a record |
| `files_for_entity` | `files:read` | Files on a record |

`file_share_record` records a share. It does not deliver the file.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/assets` | List or create an asset |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/assets/:id` | Read or update one asset |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/assets/:id/versions` | Add a version |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/assets/:id/current` | Set the current version |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/brands` | Brand picker on the create form |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/files` | File metadata |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/files/:id/url` | Short-lived download URL |

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reads need `files:read`. Writes, including asset create and version add, need `files:write`. These writes are token-only on the MCP path. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `marketing_asset_create` after `file_commit` has a file id, then add a version.

```json
{
  "tool": "marketing_asset_create",
  "arguments": {
    "title": "Data quality one-pager",
    "slug": "data-quality-one-pager",
    "kind": "one-pager"
  }
}
```

Expected result: an asset row with no current file yet. `marketing_asset_version_add` with that asset id and a committed `file_id` attaches version 1. `marketing_asset_list` then returns the title. The bytes are never inlined in the tool result.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "title": "Data quality one-pager",
  "slug": "data-quality-one-pager"
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/campaigns

# Campaigns

## What it does

Campaigns group a sales motion so members, products, and the ICP you are aiming at stay on one record.

Open **Campaigns** (`/campaigns`). `campaign_type` is `outbound_marketing` or `internal_initiative`. Status is `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `completed`, or `archived`. People on the motion, and the intake queue, are on [Pipeline](/docs/features/pipeline). Deals that belong to the motion are on [Deals](/docs/features/deals).

The list only calls the session API. A signed-in person can create a campaign through the entity route. Agents change membership, products, and ICP with the tools below.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign_list` | `campaigns:read` | List campaigns |
| `campaign_members_list` | `campaigns:read` | Members of one campaign |
| `campaign_member_add` | `campaigns:write` | Add a contact or an account |
| `campaign_member_update` | `campaigns:write` | Change member status and merge SDR metadata |
| `campaign_products_list` | `campaigns:read` | Products linked to the campaign |
| `campaign_product_link` | `campaigns:write` | Link or unlink a product |
| `campaign_icp_set` | `campaigns:write` | Attach ICP profiles |

`campaign_member_update` merges `metadata_sdr`. It does not replace that object blindly.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/campaigns` | List on this screen |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/entities/campaigns` | Create from a signed-in session |
| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | `/cockpit/api/entities/campaigns/:id` | Drawer read, update, delete |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/campaigns/:id/products` | Products on the campaign |
| `DELETE` | `/cockpit/api/campaigns/:id/products/:productId` | Unlink a product |

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reads need `campaigns:read`. Membership, product, and ICP writes need `campaigns:write`. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `campaign_member_add` with the campaign and either a contact or an account, not both as a guess.

```json
{
  "tool": "campaign_member_add",
  "arguments": {
    "campaign_id": "campaign-1",
    "contact_id": "contact-1"
  }
}
```

Expected result: one member row. Listing with `campaign_members_list` returns that contact. Adding the same pair again does not create a second membership.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "campaign_id": "campaign-1",
  "contact_id": "contact-1"
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/pipeline

# Pipeline

## What it does

Pipeline shows who is in a motion, so a member, a prospect, and an inbound intake row stay distinct.

Open **Pipeline** (`/pipeline`). Three tabs:

- **Members** — contacts or accounts on a campaign, with a member status.
- **Prospects** — CRM leads in the campaign motion.
- **Intake** — inbound rows. This tab has no New button. It is a queue you read.

This is not the deal board. Deal stages live on [Deals](/docs/features/deals). The motion itself is a [Campaign](/docs/features/campaigns).

The screen only calls the session API. It reads one session route. Adding a member is `campaign_member_add`.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign_members_list` | `campaigns:read` | Members of one campaign |
| `campaign_member_add` | `campaigns:write` | Add a contact or an account |
| `campaign_member_update` | `campaigns:write` | Update status and merge SDR metadata |
| `contact_intake` | `contacts:write`, `accounts:write` | Create a contact and account from an intake payload |

`campaign_member_update` merges `metadata_sdr`. It does not replace that object.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/pipeline` | Members, prospects, and intake for this screen |

The response is `{ "ok": true, "members": [], "prospects": [], "intake": [] }`. There is no POST on this route. Writes go through the member tools or the entity drawer.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reading members needs `campaigns:read`. Adding or updating a member needs `campaigns:write`. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `campaign_member_update` to move a member forward without wiping SDR notes already stored.

```json
{
  "tool": "campaign_member_update",
  "arguments": {
    "member_id": "member-1",
    "member_status": "working",
    "metadata_sdr": {
      "last_touch": "intro-sent"
    }
  }
}
```

Expected result: that member's status is `working`, and `metadata_sdr.last_touch` is set. Keys you did not send stay as they were.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "member_id": "member-1",
  "member_status": "working"
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/deals

# Deals

## What it does

Deals show every opportunity by stage, so you can see what is moving and update the forecast from the same board.

Two screens use the word pipeline. They are different objects.

| Screen | Route | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| **Deals** | `/sales` | Deal records, as a board by stage or as a table |
| **Pipeline** | `/pipeline` | Campaign members, CRM prospects, and intake |

**Campaigns** (`/campaigns`) are the motions those members belong to. **Products** (`/products`) are the catalog you can hang on a deal or a campaign.

## Deals

The board columns are the stage check constraint, in order:

1. Lead
2. Qualification
3. Discovery
4. Value Proposition
5. Proposal
6. Negotiate
7. Contract
8. Closed Won
9. Closed Lost

Stage values are Title Case. A deal also has `status`: `open`, `won`, `lost`, or `stalled`. `closed` becomes true for Closed Won and Closed Lost.

You can filter by domain, campaign, and account, hide closed deals, and hide deals whose campaign is excluded from the board. **New deal** creates a record. Dragging a card changes its stage. The drawer edits the rest.

Forecast fields:

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `forecast_category` | `pipeline`, `best_case`, `most_likely`, `commit` |
| `forecast_percentage` | 0–100 |

Narrative fields on the deal are `deal_summary`, `deal_details`, `product_offering`, `strategic_questions`, and `next_steps`. `scorecard` is a JSON object. Agents write that pack with `deal_scorecard_set` (scope `deals:write`). People edit the same fields in the drawer.

Line items are `deal_line_item_set` / `deal_line_items_list`, and in the app under the deal's line-item routes. Each line has a product, name, quantity, and unit amount.

Creating or renaming a **product** files a human-only approval (`product_create`, `product_rename`). Updating other product fields can go through `product_upsert`. The catalog screen is [Products](/docs/features/products).

## Proposals from activity

Ingest can store a proposed deal name on an activity without creating the deal. `deal_proposals` lists those names. `deal_proposal_resolve` approves or dismisses one. Approving is what creates the deal path. The agent does not insert the deal row on its own.

## Campaign pipeline

Members, prospects, and intake are [Pipeline](/docs/features/pipeline). The motion those members belong to is a [Campaign](/docs/features/campaigns). ICP definitions are [ICP](/docs/features/icp).

## Accounts behind the deal

Deal cards can name `account_id` plus `end_customer_account_id`, `bill_to_account_id`, and `referring_partner_account_id`. Send an id or a slug. The allowed deal fields are listed in [Entity fields](/docs/reference/entity-fields).

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `deals_list` | `deals:read` | List deals, including forecast and scorecard fields |
| `deal_scorecard_set` | `deals:write` | Write scorecard JSON and the narrative fields |
| `deal_line_items_list` | `deals:read` | Lines on a deal |
| `deal_line_item_set` | `deals:write` | Upsert one line |
| `deal_proposals` | `deals:read` | Proposed names that are not deals yet |
| `deal_proposal_resolve` | `deals:write` | Approve or dismiss a proposed name |

The board itself reads the session route below. Stage changes from a drag are a session PATCH, not a separate tool.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/sales` | Deal list for this screen. The board asks for `limit=500` |
| `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/entities/deals/:id` | Stage change and drawer edits |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/deals/:id/line-items` | Lines |
| `PATCH`, `DELETE` | `/cockpit/api/deals/:id/line-items/:itemId` | Update or remove a line |

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reads need `deals:read`. Scorecard, line, and proposal writes need `deals:write`. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `deal_scorecard_set` with the narrative you want on the deal. Omit fields you are not changing.

```json
{
  "tool": "deal_scorecard_set",
  "arguments": {
    "deal_id": "deal-1",
    "next_steps": "Send the revised scope."
  }
}
```

Expected result: those fields update on the deal the token may see. `deals_list` returns the new `next_steps`. A deal outside the caller's RLS scope is not updated.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "deal_id": "deal-1",
  "next_steps": "Send the revised scope."
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/products

# Products

## What it does

Products are the catalog, so a deal line and a campaign link both point at one definition of what you sell.

Open **Products** (`/products`). Filter by status and product line, search by name, and create or archive from the board. A signed-in person creates a product directly on this screen. An agent does not get that shortcut. `product_upsert` files a human-only approval for a create (`product_create`) or a rename (`product_rename`). Other field updates can go through in the same tool.

Line items on a deal are edited from the deal, with `deal_line_item_set`. Linking a product to a campaign is `campaign_product_link`.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `product_list` | `products:read` | List. Filters: `status`, `product_line`, `q`, `limit` |
| `product_get` | `products:read` | One product by id or slug |
| `product_upsert` | `products:write` | Create, rename, or update. Create and rename file a human-only card |
| `deal_line_item_set` | `deals:write` | Upsert a line on a deal |
| `deal_line_items_list` | `deals:read` | Lines on a deal |
| `campaign_product_link` | `campaigns:write` | Link or unlink a product on a campaign |

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/products` | List, or create from a signed-in session (no approval card) |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/products/:id` | Read, or update fields such as status |

`GET` accepts `status`, `product_line`, and `q`. The session POST is the human path. Agents use `product_upsert`.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reads need `products:read`. Agent writes need `products:write`, and a create or rename still waits on a person because those card types are human-only. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `product_upsert` with a new name and no id.

```json
{
  "tool": "product_upsert",
  "arguments": {
    "name": "Quality assessment",
    "slug": "quality-assessment",
    "product_line": "assess",
    "status": "active"
  }
}
```

Expected result: no catalog row yet. A pending `product_create` card is filed. The product appears on `/products` after a person approves it. A later `product_upsert` that changes the description on the existing id updates the row. A later call that changes the name files `product_rename` instead.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "approval": {
    "item_type": "product_create",
    "status": "pending"
  }
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/desks

# Desks

## What it does

Desks are the projects work hangs on, so a task, a routine, and a workflow template all have a home.

Open **Desks** (`/desks`). **Team** is the org view. **List** is the project table. `?view=team` or `?view=list` picks one, and the choice is remembered in the browser. A desk is a project row. Routines and workflow templates bind to a desk so scheduled work has somewhere to land.

The screen only calls the project routes. A desk is still a project row. Desk memory is its own append-only table (`desk_memory`). The scratch pad is `projects.agent_state.scratchpad`. Agents pass `project_id` on tasks and templates, and `desk_id` (the same project id) on the desk tools below.

Desk isolation is a convention, not a security boundary. An admin sees every desk. A member sees desks they own. The database does not bind a runtime to a single desk.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `task_list` | `tasks:read` | Tasks on a desk. Filter `project_id` |
| `task_create` | `tasks:write` | Create a backlog task on a desk |
| `entity_field_write` | `graph:write` | Write one project field through provenance |
| `entity_state_get` | none (token still required) | Read `agent_state` on `projects` |
| `entity_state_set` | `projects:write` | Replace `agent_state` |
| `entity_state_patch` | `projects:write` | Shallow-merge `agent_state` |
| `workflow_template_create` | `workflows:write` | Save a template bound to `project_id` |
| `workflow_apply` | `workflows:write` | Instantiate that template into tasks on a desk |
| `desk_scratchpad_get` | `projects:read` | Read the scratch pad |
| `desk_scratchpad_set` | `projects:write` | Overwrite the scratch pad (16 KiB, `expected_updated_at` conflict check) |
| `desk_memory_append` | `projects:write` | Append a desk memory row. Nothing is deleted |
| `desk_memory_list` | `projects:read` | Pinned rows plus the last 30 days (`days`, `include_all`) |
| `desk_memory_pin` | `projects:write` | Pin or unpin a memory row |
| `desk_context_get` | `projects:read` | Scratch pad and memory together |
| `task_pickup` | `tasks:write`, `comments:read` | Claim, comments, and `desk_context` |

`entity_notes` is for entity and meeting notes. Desk memory is not written there. A daily job sets `archived_at` on unpinned rows older than 30 days. Pinned rows stay. A list does not archive. The session user is the actor. A caller-supplied user id is trusted only for the service client. The server stamps who wrote the pad. Memory rows do not take a caller-supplied runtime id.

The scratch pad and the memory list are dedicated Scratch and Memory tabs on the project entity drawer. Admins and the desk owner can read and write them. Anyone else sees a no-access state. An empty scratch pad says so. An empty memory list says so.

`workflow_apply` takes `context_project_id` for the desk the new tasks should land on.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/projects` | List view |
| `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/projects/:id` | Update a project from the list or the team view |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/org-structure` | Team view |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/entities/projects/:id` | Drawer read and update |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/projects/:id/desk` | Drawer scratch pad and desk memory |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/entities/projects` | Create from a signed-in session |

Project actions also live under `/cockpit/api/projects/:id` for child counts and for convert, delete, merge, owner, and undo-delete.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Task reads need `tasks:read`. Project field state needs `projects:write`. Template writes need `workflows:write` and are token-only. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `task_create` with the desk you want the work on. Set `human_approval_to_close` on purpose. The default is false.

```json
{
  "tool": "task_create",
  "arguments": {
    "title": "Send the revised scope",
    "project_id": "desk-1",
    "human_approval_to_close": true
  }
}
```

Expected result: a backlog task on that project. It does not wake a runtime until it moves to `todo`. Because the flag is true, closing it later opens a card instead of finishing on its own.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "backlog",
  "title": "Send the revised scope",
  "human_approval_to_close": true
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/tasks

# Tasks

## What it does

Tasks are the unit of work on a board, so a person and an agent share one status line and one close rule.

Open **Tasks** (`/tasks`). Statuses are `backlog`, `todo`, `doing`, `review`, `stuck`, `done`, and `cancelled`. A task belongs to a desk (a project) and can be assigned to a person or a runtime. Moving it to `todo` is what wakes a runtime. The board only calls the session API: it lists and patches, and the stage changes go through the same transitions the MCP tools use.

`human_approval_to_close` is the close gate. On means a person must accept a close card. Off, the default, means the assignee can finish it. Set the flag when you create the task. Words in the description do not change it.

A close-gated task closes when a person approves its close card. Approving merges the linked pull requests, then closes the task. A task that is not close-gated merges a ready pull request when the assignee closes it. See [GitHub](/docs/features/github) for the merge rules.

Hidden tasks stay off the default list until `hidden_until`. Pass `include_hidden` to see them.

## Due dates and links

**Due dates.** Give a task a due date when you create it, or change it later with `task_set_due` or `task_update`. `YYYY-MM-DD` means the end of that day in Pacific time. A full ISO-8601 timestamp is used as given. Passing `null` clears it.

**Links.** A task can point at the records it is about: an account, a deal, a campaign, and contacts. Pass `account_id`, `deal_id`, `campaign_id`, and `contact_ids` on `task_create` or `task_update`. `related_entities` is the same thing as a list of `{ entity_type, entity_id }`. chytr checks each record exists before it links it. On `task_update`, a `contact_ids` list replaces the current set and an empty list clears it. Links show on the task in chytr and filter `task_list`.

A linked pull request is a link too. See [GitHub](/docs/features/github).

What you can see on the board follows [What a member can see](/docs/features/users#what-a-member-can-see).

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `task_create` | `tasks:write` | Create a backlog task |
| `task_list` | `tasks:read` | List. Hidden rows stay out unless `include_hidden` is true |
| `task_hide` | `tasks:write` | Set or clear `hidden_until` |
| `task_claim` | `tasks:write` | Claim `todo` tasks for a runtime |
| `task_claim_work_item` | `tasks:write` | Claim the one task a work item points at |
| `task_pickup` | `tasks:write`, `comments:read` | Claim plus comments. Acks unread handoffs |
| `task_start` | `tasks:write` | `todo` to `doing` |
| `task_complete` | `tasks:write` | Finish a `todo` or `doing` task that is not close-gated |
| `task_request_close` | `tasks:write` | Close. A human gate opens a card. Otherwise the task can complete |
| `task_request_promote` | `tasks:write` | Ask a person to move backlog work up |
| `task_stuck` | `tasks:write` | Mark stuck |
| `task_resume` | `tasks:write` | `stuck` to `todo`. Refuses unmet dependencies |
| `task_demote` | `tasks:write` | `todo` back to `backlog` |
| `task_reopen` | `tasks:write` | Reopen a `done` task |
| `task_cancel` | `tasks:write` | Cancel from an active status. Reason required |
| `task_reassign` | `tasks:reassign` | Reassign. Handoff comment required |
| `task_set_due` | `tasks:write` | Set or clear a task's due date |
| `task_update` | `tasks:write` | Change title, description, priority, due date, hidden date, desk, metadata, parent, and linked records. Not status, close gate, or assignee |

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks` | List or create |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id` | Read or update routing fields |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/start` | `todo` to `doing` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/complete` | Complete when not close-gated |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/request-close` | Open the close path |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/promote` | Ask to move a backlog task up |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/stuck` | Mark stuck |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/resume` | `stuck` to `todo` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/demote` | `todo` to `backlog` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/reopen` | Reopen from `done` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/cancel` | Cancel |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/archive` | Archive |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/approve-review` | Accept a task in `review` |

The board also reads `/cockpit/api/runtimes`, `/cockpit/api/accounts`, and `/cockpit/api/projects` to fill the filters.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Listing needs `tasks:read`. Stage changes need `tasks:write`. Reassign needs `tasks:reassign`. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `task_list` for the desk you are working, then `task_request_close` only for a task you were assigned.

```json
{
  "tool": "task_list",
  "arguments": {
    "project_id": "desk-1",
    "status": "doing",
    "limit": 20
  }
}
```

Expected result: doing tasks on that desk that this token's owner is allowed to see. Hidden tasks are absent. Closing one of them with `task_request_close` returns `ok` true and moves it to `done` when `human_approval_to_close` is false. When the flag is true, the task stays open and a close card is pending.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "tasks": [
    {
      "title": "Send the revised scope",
      "status": "doing",
      "human_approval_to_close": false
    }
  ]
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/work-items

# Work items

## What it does

Work items are the lease an agent holds while it runs, so you can see who has the work and whether the lease is still alive.

Open **Work Items** (`/work-items`). The board is a read-only ledger: kind, ref, status, who claimed it, last heartbeat, repo, and branch. People read it. Agents write it. A second clock-in for the same kind and ref conflicts with the live lease instead of creating a twin.

The screen only reads one session route. Clock-in, heartbeat, log, block, and clock-out are MCP tools.

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `work_clock_in` | `work:write` | Claim a lease. A live lease on the same kind and ref conflicts |
| `work_set_session` | `work:write` | Record repo, branch, and session URL |
| `work_heartbeat` | `work:write` | Extend the lease |
| `work_log` | `work:write` | Append a log line and bump the heartbeat |
| `work_block` | `work:write` | Mark blocked. `gap_type` is `policy`, `data`, or `tool` |
| `work_clock_out` | `work:write` | Release. Status `done`, `failed`, or `skipped` |
| `work_status` | `work:read` | Read by exactly one selector |

`work_status` takes `work_item_id`, or `kind` plus `ref`, or `run_id`. Send one selector.

`task_claim_work_item` and `task_pickup` claim the task the lease points at. They are task tools, listed on [Tasks](/docs/features/tasks).

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/work-items` | Ledger for this screen. Optional `status` and `limit` |

There is no POST on this route. Agents mutate leases only through the MCP tools.

## Permissions

Token scopes come from one permission-set layer. Reading a lease needs `work:read`. Clock-in and the rest of the write tools need `work:write`. The screen uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own.

## Agent example

Call `work_clock_in` when a run starts, then `work_status` with the same kind and ref.

```json
{
  "tool": "work_clock_in",
  "arguments": {
    "kind": "task",
    "ref": "desk-1:send-scope",
    "agent_id": "runtime-1",
    "run_id": "run-1",
    "lease_ttl_minutes": 30
  }
}
```

Expected result: a claimed lease. A second clock-in with the same kind and ref, while this lease is live, returns a conflict and does not replace it. `work_clock_out` with `status` `done` releases it, and the board shows that status after refresh.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "kind": "task",
  "ref": "desk-1:send-scope",
  "status": "claimed"
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/pull-requests

# Pull requests

## What it does

Pull requests show which change is still open, so a finished task is not left attached to a branch nobody merged.

Open **PRs** (`/pull-requests`). The board lists pull requests and can check one in against a task. Connecting GitHub is what makes the list real. That connection lives on [Integrations](/docs/features/integrations).

When an agent finishes a task with `task_request_close` and `human_approval_to_close` is false, a linked pull request that is open with green checks can be merged as a merge commit as part of that close. A close-gated task waits for a person, and approving its close card merges the linked pull requests before the task closes. The close rule is on [Tasks](/docs/features/tasks). Merge rules, branches, and labels are on [GitHub](/docs/features/github).

The screen only calls the session API. There is no MCP tool whose name is pull request.

## MCP tools

No pull-request tool is in the MCP catalog. The agent path that touches a linked pull request is `task_request_close` (`tasks:write`). Pass `pr_url` when you want that close to consider the linked request. The tool merges only when the task is not close-gated, the request is open, checks are green, and GitHub is connected. Otherwise it reports why and leaves the request unmerged.

`work_set_session` records the repo and branch on the lease. It does not open a pull request.

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/pull-requests` | List for this screen |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/pull-requests` | Record a pull request |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/pull-requests/check-in` | Attach the request to the open task it closes |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/work-items` | Leases shown next to the requests |

Task merge state is also on `GET` and `POST /cockpit/api/tasks/:id/merge-gate`.

## Permissions

The screen uses the signed-in session. `task_request_close` needs `tasks:write` from one permission-set layer. GitHub access is the workspace integration, not a scope on the token.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own. See [What a member can see](/docs/features/users#what-a-member-can-see).

## Agent example

Call `task_request_close` with the task and the pull request URL. Do not call a merge tool. There isn't one.

```json
{
  "tool": "task_request_close",
  "arguments": {
    "task_ids": ["task-1"],
    "pr_url": "https://github.com/example/app/pull/18",
    "note": "Scope doc matches the branch."
  }
}
```

Expected result when the task is not close-gated and the request is open with green checks: `ok` true, the request merged as a merge commit, and the task `done`. When the task is close-gated, the task stays open and a close card is pending. When checks are red, nothing merges and the result says why.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "done"
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/features/github

# GitHub

## What it does

chytr keeps each task next to its pull request. A task does not close while its change sits unmerged.

Connect GitHub once on [Integrations](/docs/features/integrations). After that, chytr reads pull requests and their check results, links them to tasks, and can merge them when a task closes. Connecting GitHub does not create users and does not grant MCP scopes.

## How a pull request links to a task

A pull request is linked to a task in any of these ways:

- An agent passes `pr_url` to `task_request_close`. The tool records the link before it looks at the task.
- A person pastes the pull request URL when moving a task to **Review** in the task drawer.
- A work item registers the pull request (`work_register_pr`, or the `prs` list on clock-out). The task picks it up through its work item.

Linking is idempotent. The same pull request on the same task is one link, however many ways it arrived.

## See a task's pull requests and checks

- **Task drawer.** Shows the linked pull request for the task with an **Open PR** link.
- **Pull requests view** (`/pull-requests`). Lists pull requests across the connected repositories. Filter by state (open, ready, merged, closed, all) and repository. The list is a cache that chytr refreshes from GitHub, so it can lag GitHub by a short while. The cache holds no check results, so **ready** here means open and not a draft. It does not mean checks are green.
- **Check status for one task.** Check results are not shown on either screen. `GET /cockpit/api/tasks/:id/merge-gate` re-reads every linked pull request and its checks from GitHub right now and reports, per pull request, whether it is merged, ready, or blocked and why. It never merges anything.

For a merge, a pull request is **ready** only when it is open, not a draft, has no conflicts, and every check on its latest commit is green.

## Closing a task merges its pull requests

Which path runs depends on the task's `human_approval_to_close` flag.

| Task | Who closes | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Not close-gated | The assignee, with `task_request_close` | If the linked pull request is ready, it is merged and the task goes straight to `done`. No close card is created. If it is not ready, nothing merges, the task stays open, and the result says why. With no pull request, the task closes straight to `done`. |
| Close-gated | A person, on the close card | `task_request_close` moves the task to `review` and opens a close card in [Approvals](/docs/features/approvals). **Approving the card merges the linked pull requests, then closes the task.** Clicking **Close** on the board does the same. |

For a close-gated task, the person's approve or Close click is the authorization. The merge is not skipped and not automatic before that click.

### Merge commit only, all or nothing

- Every merge is a **merge commit**. chytr never squashes, so each change keeps its own history.
- A task with more than one pull request is **all or nothing** at the check stage. chytr re-checks every linked pull request first. If any one is not already merged and not ready, the whole close is refused and nothing is merged.
- Only after every pull request is merged does the task close.

## Base branches and labels

chytr merges into the base branch the pull request targets. It never squashes.

If your team uses labels such as `routine` for auto-merge, apply them only from automated pipelines, never to feature pull requests. A close-gated task asks for human review, so its pull request should not carry an auto-merge label.

## When a merge fails

A refused close returns HTTP **409** with a reason. The task is not closed, and no close card is resolved. The 409's reason is `close_gated`, `prs_not_ready` or `merge_failed`; each blocking PR in `blocking[]` carries one of the reasons below.

| Reason | What to do |
|---|---|
| `draft` | Mark the pull request ready for review. |
| `conflicting` | Resolve the conflict or branch-protection requirement, then retry. This also covers GitHub's `blocked` state, such as a missing required review. |
| `close_flip_failed` | HTTP **500**, not 409: the merge succeeded but the task did not flip to `done`. Retry the close; the merged pull request is seen as merged. |
| `checks_red` | Fix or wait for the failing checks, then retry. |
| `no_checks` | No checks have reported on the head commit. Wait for CI to start, then retry. |
| `pr_fetch_failed_<status>` | chytr could not read the pull request from GitHub; the suffix is the HTTP status. Check access, then retry. |
| `no_head_sha` | GitHub returned no head commit for the pull request. Retry in a moment. |
| `merge_response_not_merged` | GitHub answered the merge call but did not report the pull request as merged. Check it on GitHub, then retry. |
| `close_gated` | The task needs human approval to close. Use the Approvals or Close button. |
| `prs_not_ready` | One or more linked pull requests are not ready. The detail lists each one's reason. |
| `merge_failed` | The merge did not complete. The detail carries the cause. |
| `mergeability_pending` | GitHub is still computing. Retry in a moment. chytr does not raise a callout for this. |
| `not_open` | The pull request was closed without merging. Reopen it or link the right one. |
| `merge_rejected` | GitHub refused the merge. The detail carries GitHub's message. |
| `github_app_unavailable` | GitHub is not connected, or its access failed. Reconnect on Integrations. |

If a merge fails partway through a task with several pull requests, the ones already merged stay merged. A retry sees them as merged and continues.

A close-gated task keeps its close card **pending** after a failure, so the card is the record that someone tried. For a task that is not close-gated, chytr also raises a notification for a non-transient block, at most once every six hours per task.

## MCP tools

No tool is named for GitHub. The tool that reaches a pull request is `task_request_close` (`tasks:write`), described on [Tasks](/docs/features/tasks). Pass `pr_url` to link and merge in the same call.

## HTTP endpoints

All of these use the signed-in session. A personal access token cannot call them.

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
