The shell search calls `GET /cockpit/api/global-search`. After two characters it returns name matches, up to five per group:

- tasks, by title
- accounts, by name
- contacts, by full name
- deals, by name

A short id (`T…` for a task, `W…` for a work item) resolves through `GET /cockpit/api/short-id` when the query matches that pattern. Results open the record. This path is a scoped `ilike` lookup. It does not embed the query and it does not search mail bodies.

`GET /cockpit/api/records/search` and `GET /cockpit/api/accounts/search` are the same style of lookup for pickers inside the app.

## Semantic search

Indexed text (activities and entity notes that passed the quality gate) is embedded with `gte-small` at 384 dimensions and stored in `rag_chunks`. Query time combines keyword search and vector search, then fuses the lists.

You use that index from:

- `/chat`, the knowledge-graph chat
- the approval deck's card chat
- MCP `search`, `rag_search`, and `entity_context_query` (scope `rag:read`)

`search` is the one to call from an agent. It routes the question, then runs the hybrid query. Optional filters are `domain_name`, `deal_name`, and `project_name`. Results are limited to the token's owner and team.

`rag_search` is the lower-level hybrid call: `query`, `match_count`, optional `source_tables`, and a time window. `entity_match_search` resolves a person, company, or campaign name to candidates. It does not merge them. `entity_search_diag` explains a name that did not resolve. `entity_context_query` builds a pack for one entity: the card, scoped chunks, and optional tasks and notes.

Digest and noise activities are not indexed. A record you cannot find in chat may still show up in the top bar if its name matches.

## What search will not do

Name search will not invent a link between a person and an account. Matching a first name is not a merge. Create and merge stay on approval cards. See [Approvals](/docs/features/approvals).

## MCP tools

| Tool | Scope | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `search` | `rag:read` | Scoped hybrid search. This is the one to call |
| `rag_search` | `rag:read` | Lower-level hybrid call |
| `entity_match_search` | `rag:read` | Name to candidates. Does not merge |
| `entity_search_diag` | `rag:read` | Why a name did not resolve |
| `entity_context_query` | `rag:read` | Card, scoped chunks, optional tasks and notes |

## HTTP endpoints

| Method | Path | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/global-search` | Top-bar name search. Query `q`, after two characters |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/short-id` | Resolve a short id when the query matches that pattern |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/records/search` | Picker lookup |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/accounts/search` | Account picker lookup |

Chat on `/chat` and the deck card chat call the semantic index from the session. They are not a third search engine.

## Permissions

Semantic tools need `rag:read` from one permission-set layer. Results are limited to the token's owner and team. The top bar uses the signed-in session.

Row access is RLS by creator. Admins see all rows. Members see their own. Name search does not bypass that.

## Agent example

Call `search` with the question you would type. Add a dimension filter only when you already know it.

```json
{
  "tool": "search",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "what did we agree about rollout scope",
    "match_count": 5
  }
}
```

Expected result: fused keyword and vector hits from indexed text the token may see. Digest and noise activities are absent. A name that exists only as a CRM row, with no indexed text, can still appear in `GET /cockpit/api/global-search` and be missing here.

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "matches": [
    {
      "summary": "Scoped the rollout to one region."
    }
  ]
}
```

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/reference/mcp-tools

# MCP tools

Agents call `POST /api/mcp` with a bearer token. This page lists every tool in the MCP manifest: name, required scope, what it is for, and the parameters that matter. Scopes are copied from the manifest. A tool runs only when the token includes every required scope.

Empty scopes are written as `none`. The call still needs a valid token. Dynamic scopes are checked against the table you pass.

Human-only approval types cannot be approved here. See [Permissions and API keys](/docs/reference/permissions). How to connect a runtime is in [Connecting agents](/docs/features/agents).

Parameter lists are the fields callers actually send. Optional fields are included when they change behavior. Servers ignore unknown keys.

## Search

| Tool | Scope | Purpose | Key parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rag_search` | `rag:read` | Hybrid keyword and vector search over indexed chunks. | `query`, `match_count`, `source_tables`, `since`, `until` |
| `entity_match_search` | `rag:read` | Resolve a person, company, or campaign name to candidates. Does not merge. | `query`, `limit`, `entity_types` |
| `search` | `rag:read` | Scoped hybrid search with an intent router and optional dimension filters. | `query`, `match_count`, `offset`, `source_tables`, `domain_name`, `deal_name`, `project_name`, `skip_router` |
| `entity_search_diag` | `rag:read` | Explain why a name did not resolve. | `canonical_name` |
| `entity_context_query` | `rag:read` | Pack one entity's card, scoped chunks, and optional tasks and notes for a question. | `question`, `entity_type`, `entity_id` or `entity_name`, `include_tasks`, `include_activities`, `include_notes` |

## Activities

|---|---|---|---|
| `timeline_for_entity` | `activities:read, mentions:read` | Activity timeline for one CRM record. | `entity_type`, `entity_id`, `limit`, `occurred_after`, `occurred_before` |
| `activity_timeline` | `activities:read` | Owner-wide activity feed with keyset pagination. | `occurred_after`, `occurred_before`, `type`, `work_type`, `source`, `exclude_noise`, `limit`, `cursor` |
| `activity_create` | `activities:write` | Create or upsert an activity. | `type`, `summary`, `content`, `source`, `source_id`, `occurred_at`, `raw_payload` |
| `mention_add` | `mentions:write, activities:write` | Link an activity to an entity. | `activity_id`, `entity_type`, `entity_id` |

Returns `new`, `reuse`, `skip_existing_member`, or `uncertain`. Never auto-merges. | `campaign_id`, `name`, `domain`, `account_id` |

## Approvals

| Tool | Scope | Purpose | Key parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| `approval_create` | `approvals:write` | Create a pending approval. Entity creates must send `on_approve` or `table` and `fields`. | `item_type`, `title`, `summary`, `table`, `fields`, `on_approve`, `metadata` |
| `approval_list` | `approvals:read` | List approvals. | `limit`, `status` |
| `approval_resolve` | `approvals:write` | Resolve an approval. A user session records that user as human. A PAT records the token as agent. A session cannot forge the agent identity. Human-only types can be approved only by an owner or admin. | `id`, `status` (`approved`, `rejected`, `deferred`), `decision_notes` |

## Extraction

Extraction is headless. These tools are the review contract. Inputs, outputs, thresholds, and the approve path are in [Meetings and extraction](/docs/features/meetings).

| Tool | Scope | Purpose | Key parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extraction_pending` | `approvals:read` | List pending `extraction.%` rows for the caller. Returns an array of `id`, `item_type`, `title`, `summary`, `proposed_payload`, `agent_irac`, `agent_skill_versions`, `created_at`. | `action_type`, `limit` (default 20, max 100), `offset` |
| `extraction_review` | `approvals:write` | Approve or reject one card through `resolve_approval`. A session records human. A PAT records agent. Approve runs `on_approve`. Reject applies nothing. | `approval_id`, `decision`, `note` |
| `extraction_review_bulk` | `approvals:write` | Resolve up to `limit` pending rows of one action type for the caller (default 20, max 100). Returns `{ ok, action_type, decision, updated, results }`. | `action_type`, `decision`, `note`, `limit` |
| `extraction_threshold_set` | `approvals:write` | Set the auto-pass threshold (0 to 1). Also requires an admin: `is_admin()` for a session, `is_admin_for` for a token. | `action_type`, `threshold` |
| `extraction_metrics` | `approvals:read` | Counts and agreement rate by action type, for the caller, over `days` (default 30). | `days` |

List, bulk, and metrics filter `owner_user_id` to the caller. A router card's `on_approve` is `extraction_apply`, so approve applies the proposal. A failed apply leaves the card pending. Direct apply, before a card exists, is limited to `enrich_fact` and `new_mention`, and only when the threshold is below `1.0`.

Takes a due date and links to an account, deal, campaign, or contacts. | `title`, `description`, `project_id`, `assignee_type`, `assignee_id`, `domain`, `human_approval_to_close`, `priority`, `hidden_until`, `due_date`, `account_id`, `deal_id`, `campaign_id`, `contact_ids`, `related_entities`, `links`, `tag_slugs` |

A `contact_ids` list replaces the linked contacts. | `task`, `title`, `description`, `priority`, `due_date`, `hidden_until`, `project_id`, `metadata`, `parent_task_id`, `account_id`, `deal_id`, `campaign_id`, `contact_ids`, `related_entities`, `actor` |

## Desks

`desk_id` is the project id. Desk isolation is a convention, not a security boundary: an admin sees every desk, and a member sees desks they own. The scratch pad is overwritten in place (16 KiB). Desk memory is append-only. A daily job archives unpinned rows older than 30 days. Nothing is deleted. `entity_notes` is not used for desk memory. The server stamps the writer. Callers do not pass a runtime id or a written-by name. A member who passes another user's id is refused.

| Tool | Scope | Purpose | Key parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| `desk_scratchpad_get` | `projects:read` | Read the scratch pad and its `updated_at`. | `desk_id` |
| `desk_scratchpad_set` | `projects:write` | Overwrite the scratch pad. Stale `expected_updated_at` returns `conflict`. The server stamps the writer. | `desk_id`, `text`, `expected_updated_at` |
| `desk_memory_append` | `projects:write` | Append one memory row. The server leaves the runtime id empty. | `desk_id`, `body` |
| `desk_memory_list` | `projects:read` | Pinned rows plus the last `days` (default 30). `include_all` adds archived rows. | `desk_id`, `days`, `include_all` |
| `desk_memory_pin` | `projects:write` | Pin or unpin one row. Pinning keeps it out of the archive. | `desk_id`, `memory_id`, `pinned` |
| `desk_context_get` | `projects:read` | Scratch pad and memory list together. Same shape `task_pickup` returns. | `desk_id`, `days`, `include_all` |

## Classifiers

Question sets are content-hashed. An edit appends a version. `bool` is stored as `noul`. New flows start disabled. Archiving a flow is a soft delete; a flow with no owner can only be archived by an admin session. Usage stats stay on the signed-in HTTP route and have no MCP tool.

| Tool | Scope | Purpose | Key parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| `classifier_flows_list` | `classifiers:read` | List flows and question-set versions. `can_edit` is true when the caller may write. Archived flows are hidden unless `include_archived` is true. | `include_archived` |
| `classifier_flow_get` | `classifiers:read` | Read one flow and its versions. | `flow_key` |
| `classifier_flow_create` | `classifiers:write` | Create a flow and its first pinned question set. Closed answers only: choice, score, or bool. | `flow_key`, `description`, `questions`, `enabled`, `retrieval_spec`, `act_policy`, `act_allowlist` |
| `classifier_flow_update` | `classifiers:write` | Edit description, enabled, act policy, or the act allow list. Does not change the pinned set. | `flow_key`, `description`, `enabled`, `act_policy`, `act_allowlist` |
| `classifier_flow_archive` | `classifiers:write` | Archive (soft delete) a flow, or restore it with `archived` false. Archiving forces the flow disabled, so it stops running. Runs and versions are kept. Restore leaves it disabled. The caller must own the flow or be an app admin. | `flow_key`, `archived` |
| `classifier_question_set_create` | `classifiers:write` | Append a version. Identical content returns the existing version. `pin` true points the flow at it. | `flow_key`, `questions`, `retrieval_spec`, `pin` |
| `classifier_question_set_pin` | `classifiers:write` | Pin a version that already belongs to the flow. | `flow_key`, `question_set_id` |

See [Classifiers](/docs/features/classifiers).

## Skills

| Tool | Scope | Purpose | Key parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skill_list` | `approvals:read` | List skills. | `enabled_only`, `action_type`, `family`, `project_id` |

| `skill_metrics` | `approvals:read` | Recommendation agreement rates. | `days` |

| `skill_update` | `skills:write` | Update a skill and queue a re-sync. | `skill_id`, `title`, `summary`, `body_md`, `status`, `enabled` |

## LLMs

Provider tokens go to Vault and are never returned. `has_vault` is the only secret signal. A blank token on update keeps the stored secret. `model_id` must be a pinned id. The caller must also be a workspace owner or admin.

| Tool | Scope | Purpose | Key parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| `llm_provider_list` | `decisions:read` | List providers. No Vault id or token. | none |
| `llm_provider_create` | `decisions:write` | Create a provider. Optional token is stored in Vault. `enabled` defaults false. | `provider_key`, `endpoint_url`, `enabled`, `token` |
| `llm_provider_update` | `decisions:write` | Update a provider. Omit a field to leave it. Blank `token` keeps the secret. | `provider_key`, `endpoint_url`, `enabled`, `token` |
| `llm_provider_disable` | `decisions:write` | Kill switch. The Vault secret stays. | `provider_key` |
| `llm_binding_list` | `decisions:read` | List named instances and flow options. | none |
| `llm_binding_create` | `decisions:write` | Create a pinned instance. One row per flow and role. | `instance_name`, `flow_key`, `role`, `provider_key`, `model_id`, `params`, `enabled` |
| `llm_binding_update` | `decisions:write` | Update an instance by id. Omitted fields stay. | `id`, `instance_name`, `flow_key`, `role`, `provider_key`, `model_id`, `params`, `enabled` |
| `llm_binding_disable` | `decisions:write` | Kill switch. The row stays. | `id` |

See [LLMs](/docs/features/llms).

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/reference/permissions

# Permissions and API keys

One permission layer, built on permission sets, covers the app and the API. A permission set is a named bundle of scopes from the catalog `pat_scopes`. The app and a signed-in user's API token use that person's set. An agent token is a separate credential.

## Status

**Planned.** A signed-in user's API token inherits that user's full permission set, the same set the app uses.

**Today.** `app_settings.feature.permission_sets_users` defaults to off. While it is off:

- Grants in `user_permission_sets` are empty. `user_effective_scopes` returns the read-only floor (`pat_scopes.oauth_default`) and nothing from the user's sets.
- A user JWT on `POST /api/mcp` is gated by that floor. If the resolver fails, the server falls closed to the same read list.
- The chytr session is a Supabase session cookie. Row access is the database policies described under [Row access](#row-access). The session does not load the user's permission set.
- Assigning a set to a user raises while the flag is off.

Agent personal access tokens are live and are not waiting on this flag. See [Agent tokens](#agent-tokens).

## User API tokens

A user API token is a bearer for a signed-in person (a user JWT on `/api/mcp`, or a session cookie on `/cockpit/api`).

Planned behavior: the token's scopes are the user's permission set, the same set the UI is checked against. Issuing the token does not pick a second, smaller set.

Today, that inheritance is the flag above. Until it is on, a user JWT holds the read floor, and writes that are token-only stay on an agent token. Those token-only writes include `files:write`, `schedules:write`, and `workflows:write`.

## Agent tokens

An agent calls MCP with a personal access token. The value starts with `cbpat_` and is shown once at **Admin → API Keys** (`/settings/keys`). Store it outside the repo. The caller may be an agent, so the token does not inherit the user's permission set.

When you create one you set:

- a name
- one or more permission sets attached to **this token**
- extra scopes, as individual checkboxes
- a TTL: 1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days (the form default), 30 days, or forever

Effective scopes are the union of the token's active sets plus the extras, stored on `api_tokens.scopes` and recomputed when membership or extras change. That union is what the MCP server checks. You can replace set membership or edit the extras later. Revoke is immediate for new calls.

The same routes issue and edit tokens:

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tokens` | List, or issue. Plaintext is in the create response only |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tokens/:id/revoke` | Revoke |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tokens/:id/scopes` | Replace extra scopes |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tokens/:id/sets` | Replace permission-set membership |

Workflow trigger tools take the workspace from this token's binding. Do not pass `workspace_id`. A token bound to one workspace cannot name another.

## Permission sets

**Admin → Perm Sets** edits named bundles of scopes. Seeded slugs are `mcp-readonly`, `cockpit-ops`, and `crm-read`. You can change them after install. A retired scope stays in the catalog so old tokens can be understood, and it is not offered for new grants.

`GET`, `POST`, and `PATCH /cockpit/api/permission-sets` list, create, and archive sets. `GET` and `POST /cockpit/api/permission-sets/admin` are the admin operations.

## Scope catalog

A tool runs only when the caller's scopes are a superset of `required_scopes` in the MCP manifest. Dynamic tools check the table at call time (`contacts:read` versus `deals:read`, for example).

| Area | Scopes |
|---|---|
| CRM | `accounts:read` `accounts:write` `contacts:read` `contacts:write` `deals:read` `deals:write` `campaigns:read` `campaigns:write` `projects:read` `projects:write` |
| Activity | `activities:read` `activities:write` `mentions:read` `mentions:write` |
| Approvals and notes | `approvals:read` `approvals:write` `notes:read` `notes:write` |
| Search | `rag:read` |
| Tasks | `tasks:read` `tasks:write` `tasks:reassign` |
| chytr shell | `cockpit:read` `cockpit:write` `comments:read` `comments:write` |
| Work and dispatch | `work:read` `work:write` `schedules:write` `workflows:read` `workflows:write` `graph:write` |
| Files and products | `files:read` `files:write` `products:read` `products:write` |
| Goals and ICP | `charters:read` `charters:write` `metrics:read` `icp:read` `icp:write` |
| Cases and outcomes | `cases:read` `cases:write` `engagement_outcomes:read` `engagement_outcomes:write` |
| Agents | `agent_bus:read` `agent_bus:write` `skills:read` `skills:write` |
| Other catalog entries | `analysis:write` `capture:write` `decision:write` `decisions:read` `decisions:write` `voice:read` `voice:write` `marketing:analytics:read` `marketing:ig:read` `marketing:tiktok:read` `marketing:x:read` |

`leads:read` and `leads:write` are retired. Some catalog scopes have no tool on this MCP server. Holding the scope does not create a tool.

Tools with an empty `required_scopes` list (`entity_get`, `entity_state_get`) still require a valid token. Empty means no extra scope string.

## Who can approve

| Actor | Can approve |
|---|---|
| Person in chytr whose session owns the card, or `is_admin()` | That card, including human-only types. A workspace role is not `is_admin()` |
| Agent token with `approvals:write`, via `approval_resolve` or `extraction_review` | Types that are not human-only. The call stamps the actor as `agent` |

Human-only types: `graph_entity_merge`, `graph_entity_rename`, `graph_entity_create`, `graph_entity_alias`, `merge_proposal`, `stage2_identity`, `product_create`, `product_rename`, `engagement_outcome_achieve`, `workflow_cross_desk_grant`.

`is_admin()` is `user_profiles.is_admin`. It is a database flag, separate from the workspace `admin` role. It is not implied by a token scope. `extraction_threshold_set` requires it: `is_admin()` for a session, `is_admin_for` for a token. See [Meetings and extraction](/docs/features/meetings).

## Row access

A row belongs to the person who created it. Members see their own rows. Workspace admins and owners see every row. Sharing comes later. Legacy rows are backfilled with their creator.

The field that carries "created by" is `owner_user_id`. On insert, `set_owner_user_id()` stamps it from the session user when the column is null. Tables that have `team_id` get that filled in the same trigger. Tables without `team_id` use `set_owner_user_id_owner_only()`, which stamps `owner_user_id` only. A writer may set `owner_user_id` explicitly. The extraction router, when it runs, sets it to the activity's owner.

Some tables also have `created_by` as text (tasks, briefs). That string is attribution. It is not the access column. Do not send `owner_user_id` on a create card. The server stamps it. See [Entity fields](/docs/reference/entity-fields).

**Status.** This creator rule is the model. It is not the policy on every table yet.

- `approvals` uses it. A session sees or updates a row when `owner_user_id` is that user, or `is_admin()` is true, or the caller holds the matching approvals scope. Null owners were backfilled. A token with that scope can still see rows that person did not create.
- Core CRM tables (`accounts`, `contacts`, `deals`, `activities`, and the same family) still allow a row when `is_owner()` or `is_admin()` is true, or when the caller holds the matching PAT scope. That is wider than "rows I created."
- Some later tables already use `owner_user_id =` the caller, or `is_admin()` (files, and parts of the task and comment spine).
- `resolve_approval` refuses a session user who is not the row's `owner_user_id` and is not `is_admin()`. chytr's resolve routes update the row directly. The same RLS applies, and the chokepoint records the session user as human. An approve with no session, and not through `resolve_approval`, is refused.
- Extraction list, bulk review, and metrics filter to the caller's `owner_user_id` inside the tool. They do not widen for an admin.

## Workspace membership

Member administration is not an MCP scope. It is a chytr session of a workspace `owner` or `admin`. See [Users and members](/docs/features/users).

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/reference/entity-fields

# Entity fields

The database is the source of truth. Approval cards are checked against `approval_entity_shapes`, which you can edit under **Admin → Approval types**. The tables below match that shape plus the check constraints. If a later migration disagrees with this page, the migration wins.

Agents do not insert these tables directly. They submit a card (`graph_entity_create` or `graph_entity_update`) or an `entity_graph_checkin`. A person approves creates. `entity_field_write` is the single-field path for a value that already has a row, with a source of `agent`, `crm`, or `import`. `entity_create` as an MCP tool is deprecated and does not insert.

Never send these keys on a card: `tags`, `domain_wall`, `references`, `slug`, `id`, `owner_user_id`, `contacts.name`.

`owner_user_id` is the "created by" column. `set_owner_user_id()` stamps it on insert from the session user when it is null. A text `created_by` on tasks and briefs is attribution, and it is not the access column. Who can see the row is in [Permissions and API keys](/docs/reference/permissions#row-access).

Foreign keys accept an id or a slug.

## Card fields

### Accounts

Required: `name`.

Allowed: `name`, `summary`, `industry`, `website`, `domain`, `headquarters_city`, `headquarters_country`, `lifecycle_stage`, `employee_count_range`, `annual_revenue_range`, `phone`.

### Contacts

Required: `full_name`, or both `first_name` and `last_name`.

Allowed: `full_name`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `title`, `location`, `linkedin_url`, `summary`, `lifecycle_stage`, `account_id`, `phone_primary`, `seniority`.

### Deals

Required: `name`.

Allowed: `name`, `stage`, `status`, `value`, `amount_cents`, `close_date`, `account_id`, `campaign_id`, `end_customer_account_id`, `bill_to_account_id`, `referring_partner_account_id`.

### Projects

Required: `name`.

Allowed: `name`, `status`, `classification`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `account_id`, `deal_id`, `campaign_id`, `client_account_id`, `kind`, `domain`.

### Campaigns

Required: `name`, `campaign_type`.

Allowed: `name`, `campaign_type`, `status`, `description`, `goal`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `exclude_deals_from_board`.

### Territories

Required: `name`.

Allowed: `name`, `partner_account_id`, `parent_id`, `status`, `partner_fy`, `dimensions`.

`territories.status` has no check constraint. The convention used in the product is `active` or `inactive`.

## Allowed values

### Lifecycle stage (accounts and contacts)

`subscriber`, `lead`, `mql`, `sql`, `opportunity`, `customer`, `evangelist`, `churned`, `other`, `unqualified`, `active`, `lost`, `cancelled`, `needs-review`.

`prospect` is normalized to `lead` on the way in. `cancelled` is the archive value. Use `needs-review` when the name is a single token and there is no email and no account.

### Account commercial status

`customer_status` (nullable): `prospect`, `opportunity`, `customer`, `former-customer`, `lost`, `unqualified`.

`partner_status` (nullable): `evaluating`, `onboarding`, `active`, `cancelled`, `inactive`.

These two are columns on the account. They are not the lifecycle stage, and they are not both required on a create card.

### Contact kind

`contact_kind`: `person`, `automation`, `shared_inbox`, `unknown`. The database classifies this from the email and name. A user-set kind is locked against that classifier. It is not a create-card field in the shape above.

### Deals

`stage`: `Lead`, `Qualification`, `Discovery`, `Value Proposition`, `Proposal`, `Negotiate`, `Contract`, `Closed Won`, `Closed Lost`.

`status`: `open`, `won`, `lost`, `stalled`.

`forecast_category`: `pipeline`, `best_case`, `most_likely`, `commit`.

### Projects

`status`: `active`, `paused`, `stuck`, `completed`, `cancelled`.

`classification` (nullable): `internal`, `client`, `partner`.

### Campaigns

`campaign_type`: `outbound_marketing`, `internal_initiative`.

`status`: `draft`, `active`, `paused`, `completed`, `archived`.

### Tasks

`status`: `backlog`, `todo`, `doing`, `review`, `stuck`, `done`, `cancelled`.

`human_approval_to_close`: boolean. Default false.

### Approvals

`status`: `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `deferred`, `expired`, `delegated`.

### Activity quality

`quality_class`: `substantive`, `transactional`, `notification`, `digest`, `noise`.

## Agent state and notes

`entity_state_get`, `entity_state_set`, and `entity_state_patch` read or write `agent_state` on `contacts`, `accounts`, `deals`, or `projects`. Set replaces the object. Patch shallow-merges. Pass `expected_updated_at` when you need to lose the race instead of clobbering another writer.

`entity_note_add` appends a note. `entity_notes_list` returns the newest notes. Long bodies are truncated in the tool response.

# source: https://chytr.ai/docs/reference/http-api

# HTTP API

The browser calls chytr on the same host. It does not call PostgREST from the client. Handlers live under `apps/cockpit/app`.

## Auth

`/cockpit/api/*` uses the Supabase session cookie. `requireUser()` rejects a missing session. The middleware returns JSON `401` for these routes instead of redirecting to HTML. Responses are `{ "ok": true, ... }` or `{ "ok": false, "error": "..." }`.

Three routes sit outside that prefix:

| Method | Path | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/mcp` | `Authorization: Bearer` with a `cbpat_…` token or a user JWT. Proxies to the MCP Edge Function |
| `GET` | `/api/mcp` | Unauthenticated hint for OAuth metadata. Not a JSON-RPC call |
| `GET` | `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` | Public resource metadata |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/ingest` | `Authorization: Bearer` with `COCKPIT_INGEST_API_KEY`. Agent-hook log ingest. Unexpected failures still return HTTP 200 with `ok: false` |
| `POST` | `/api/gap-action` | Session. Files a pending approval for a calendar gap (`log-call`, `generate-brief`, `not-held`, `exclude`). Does not apply the action |

## Shell

| Methods | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/cockpit` | Home aggregate |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/dash` | Dash tiles |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/global-search` | Name search. Query `q` |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/short-id` | Resolve a short id |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/notifications` | Inbox |
| `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/notifications/:id` | Mark read or dismissed |

## Approvals

Extraction review uses these routes. There is no `/extraction` resource. Filter `item_type` starting with `extraction.` on the list. `PATCH` body is `{ "status": "approved" | "rejected", "note": "..." }`. Bulk body is `{ "ids": ["..."], "status": "approved" | "rejected", "note": "..." }` with 1 to 200 ids. The contract, including what approve applies, is in [Meetings and extraction](/docs/features/meetings).

| Methods | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/approvals` | Pending queue, every type, up to 500 |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id` | Read any status, or set `approved` / `rejected` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/bulk` | Bulk resolve. Returns `{ ok, updated, status }` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id/merge-approve` | Approve a merge card |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id/merge-context` | Merge context for the card |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id/close-approve` | Approve a close card |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id/reject-cancel` | Reject and cancel the linked work |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id/backlog` | Send linked work back to backlog |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/approvals/:id/task-context` | Tasks attached to the card |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/approval-shapes` | Read or edit entity shapes and type contracts |

Deck helpers, also session-authenticated: `POST /cockpit/api/deck/chat`, `POST /cockpit/api/deck/graph-chat`, `GET /cockpit/api/deck/context`, `GET /cockpit/api/deck/ground`, `POST /cockpit/api/deck/events`.

## Tasks

| Methods | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks` | List or create |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id` | Read or update |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/promote` | Ask to move a backlog task up |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/start` | `todo` to `doing` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/complete` | Complete a task that is not close-gated |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/close` | Close-gated acknowledgement |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/request-close` | Open the close path |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/stuck` | Mark stuck |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/resume` | `stuck` to `todo` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/demote` | `todo` to `backlog` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/reopen` | Reopen from `done` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/cancel` | Cancel |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/approve-review` | Accept a task that is in `review` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/archive` | Archive |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/merge-gate` | Read or act on the linked pull-request gate |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/activities` | Activity linked to the task |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/scheduled` | Create a scheduled task |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tasks/:id/schedule-enable` | Enable that schedule |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/task-tags` | Tag catalog |

## Records

`GET` list routes: `/accounts`, `/contacts`, `/sales` (deals), `/projects`, `/campaigns`, `/territories`, `/pipeline`, `/activities`, `/marketing-content`.

Search helpers: `GET /accounts/search`, `GET /records/search`.

Generic entity drawer:

| Methods | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/entities/:table` | Create through the app's entity path |
| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | `/cockpit/api/entities/:table/:id` | Read, update, delete |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/entities/:table/:id/merge` | Merge |

`POST`, `PATCH`, and `DELETE` allow `accounts`, `contacts`, `deals`, `projects`, `campaigns`, and `territories`. `GET` also opens the drawer for campaign members, prospects, marketing content, and ICP profiles.

Deal line items: `GET` and `POST /cockpit/api/deals/:id/line-items`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /cockpit/api/deals/:id/line-items/:itemId`.

Products: `GET` and `POST /products`, `GET` and `PATCH /products/:id`.

Campaign products: `GET` and `POST /campaigns/:id/products`, `DELETE /campaigns/:id/products/:productId`.

Project actions under `/projects/:id`: `GET` and `PATCH` the row, `GET …/child-counts`, and `POST` `convert`, `delete`, `merge`, `owner`, and `undo-delete`.

Cases: `GET` and `POST /cases`, `GET` and `PATCH /cases/:id`, outcomes on `/cases/:id/outcomes`.

## Workflows, agents, tokens

| Methods | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/workflows` | List or create templates |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/workflows/:id` | Read or edit |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/workflows/:id/trigger` | Enqueue a trigger |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/workflows/:id/trigger/dry-run` | Validate without starting |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/workflows/:id/trigger/events` | Trigger event log |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/runtimes` | List or upsert a runtime. `?all=1` includes disabled |
| `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/runtimes/:id` | Update. Blank secret keeps the stored one |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/runtimes/:id/disable` | Disable |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/runtimes/:id/instant-task` | Insert a todo for that runtime |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/runtimes/:id/sessions` | Sessions for the runtime |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/runtimes/binding-options` | Runtimes you can bind a job to |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/ops/jobs` | Routines. `/cockpit/api/ops/routines` is the same handlers |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/queue` | Queue and tick snapshot |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/queue/bind` | Set or clear a job's primary runtime |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/queue/heartbeat` | `bootstrap` or `run_now` |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tokens` | List tokens, or issue one. Plaintext is in the create response only |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tokens/:id/revoke` | Revoke |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tokens/:id/scopes` | Replace extra scopes |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/tokens/:id/sets` | Replace permission-set membership |
| `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/permission-sets` | List, create, archive |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/permission-sets/admin` | Admin operations on sets |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/users` | List members, or invite / change role / deactivate |

## Calendar, comments, files

| Methods | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/calendar/grid` | Calendar grid |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/timeline` | Legacy timeline payload |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/timeline/link` | Attach a note to an event |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/comments` | List or create |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/comments/:id` | Read, or ack / applied / dismiss |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/files` | File metadata |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/files/:id/url` | Short-lived download URL |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/assets` | Marketing asset registry |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/assets/:id` | One asset |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/assets/:id/versions` | Add a version |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/assets/:id/current` | Set the current version |

## Goals, ICP, health

| Methods | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/goals/charters` | Charters |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/goals/charters/:id` | One charter |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/goals/metrics` | Metric catalog |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/goals/metrics/query` | Compute one metric |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/icp-profiles` | ICP profiles |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/icp-fit-intent` | Fit and intent grid |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/icp-win-rate` | Win-rate summary |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/health` | Graph hygiene |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/pipeline-health` | Meeting-pipeline health fields |
| `GET` | `/cockpit/api/decisions/rank1` | Quality-classification audit |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/decisions/graph` | List flows, or create one. Create lands disabled with an empty act allowlist |
| `GET`, `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/decisions/graph/:flowKey` | Load or save one flow. Includes `can_edit` |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/decisions/graph/:flowKey/test` | Dry-run fixture answers. Writes nothing and calls no provider |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/llms/providers` | List providers, or create one. Optional `token` is write-only |
| `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/llms/providers/:providerKey` | Update. A blank token keeps the stored secret |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/llms/providers/:providerKey/disable` | Disable the provider. The stored token stays |
| `GET`, `POST` | `/cockpit/api/llms/bindings` | List instances and flows, or create a pinned instance |
| `PATCH` | `/cockpit/api/llms/bindings/:id` | Update an instance. Omitted fields stay |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/llms/bindings/:id/disable` | Disable the instance. The row stays |
| `POST` | `/cockpit/api/flows/:slug/start` | Start a registered flow |

## Also routed

These exist and use the same session auth. They are operational screens more than a stable integration surface: work items, pull requests, logs, runtime heatmap, agent hook stats, job liveness, deliverables health, permission health, classifiers stats, domains, brands, skill families, skills dispatch, org structure, related work, campaign members, Cursor Cloud session proxy, voice session, and c-suite tallies.

Integrations under `/cockpit/api/integrations` connect or revoke a provider and store optional Cursor and log-drain settings. Treat provider secrets as server-side only.

Voice routes (`/cockpit/api/voice/session`, `transcribe`, `tts`) need `XAI_API_KEY` on the server. They no-op in practice when the key is absent.
